items.stem: Explain the difference between the OR gate and the XOR gate.

items.stem: Explain why NAND gates are called universal gates.

items.stem: Explain how a truth table can be used to check that a logic circuit matches its problem statement.

items.stem: Explain why working columns are useful when completing a truth table for a complex expression.

items.answer: (a) 1010 (b) X = NOT C NOR (NOT A XOR B)

items.stem: A car warning light X depends on three inputs: D = 1 if a door is open, K = 1 if the key is in the ignition and B = 1 if the seat belt is fastened. The output X is 1 when it is not true that (either K is 1 or (either (K is 1 and B is 1) or D is 1 but not both) but not both). Write the logic expression for X.
items.answer: X = NOT (K XOR ((K AND B) XOR D))
items.markingKey: X = NOT (K XOR ((K AND B) XOR D)). 1 mark per correctly placed operator/gate [4]

items.stem: A machine in a factory stops (output X = 1) depending on three inputs: P = 1 if the pressure is too high, S = 1 if the safety guard is open and L = 1 if the oil level is low. The output X is 1 when ((neither P is 1 nor S is 1) or L is 1) or P is 1. (a) Write a logic expression for X. (b) Complete the truth table, giving X for PSL = 000 to 111 in order. (c) State the number of logic gates needed if each operator (including NOT) is one gate. (d) List the input combinations that make X = 1.
What is the minimum number of NAND gates needed to make an OR gate?
items.markingKey: A OR B = (A NAND A) NAND (B NAND B).

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) Explain why manufacturers often build circuits only from NAND gates. (b) Show how A OR B can be built using only NAND gates.
items.answer: (a) NAND is universal so any circuit can be built; using one gate type simplifies manufacture and NAND gates are cheap and fast in CMOS. (b) (A NAND A) gives NOT A; (B NAND B) gives NOT B; (NOT A) NAND (NOT B) = A OR B (De Morgan).
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark: universal; 1 mark: one type of chip/cheaper manufacture [2] (b) 1 mark: NOT A and NOT B from NANDs; 1 mark: final NAND; 1 mark: justification [3]

items.stem: Mei claims that the circuits X = NOT (A OR B) and X = (NOT A) OR (NOT B) are equivalent. Use a truth table or a logic argument to decide whether the claim is correct.
items.answer: Incorrect: the outputs differ for at least one input combination (e.g. A = 1, B = 0).
items.markingKey: 1 mark: evaluates both for all input rows; 1 mark: correct conclusion [2]

items.stem: A designer must replace one OR gate and one NAND gate with circuits made only from NOR gates. State the minimum number of NOR gates needed for each and the total.
items.answer: OR: 2; NAND: 4; total 6

items.stem: Noah at Eagles Sports Club has designed a circuit with output X = (NOT C OR B) NOR A. (a) Complete the truth table for ABC = 000 to 111. (b) Write a sum-of-products expression for X from your truth table. (c) Explain why a simplified circuit with the same truth table would be preferred.
items.answer: (a) 01000000 (b) X = (NOT A AND NOT B AND C) (c) fewer gates: cheaper, less power, less delay, same function
items.markingKey: (a) 0, 1, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0 [3] (b) one AND term per row where X = 1: (NOT A AND NOT B AND C) [2] (c) any two of fewer gates/cost/power/heat/speed [2]
